note: A goblet squat to a box. The catalog stocks two goblet squats — Kettlebell Goblet Cyclist Squat and Dumbbell Goblet Split Squat — but neither is this movement, and the box support is the whole point clinically. The pattern is what transfers.
The catalog's hip-lift pattern is stocked only by the two hamstring walkouts. A hip thrust is the same kinematic class and no catalog row names it.
Frontal-plane hip abduction against a loop band. Abduction appears in the catalog only as a secondary pattern on the crossback lunge, so this is the one session naming it as the primary work.
Coach shorthand for a dumbbell floor press. Horizontal push, and the floor variant is the bench-free version she can do at home.
Single-arm overhead press from half-kneeling. Vertical push; the stance is a stability choice, not a second pattern.
Scapular retraction against a band. Horizontal pull, the lightest expression of it in the catalog's vocabulary.
The catalog's only step-up is Barbell Step Up to Knee-Drive, which needs a barbell she does not own — so she did not do that exercise, but she did do that pattern.
Kettlebell RDL — a hip hinge. Shares the pattern with Hip Thrust, which is why the two lower-body sessions read as repeated hip-lift work rather than as two unrelated movements.

The only two-pattern row here, and the reason patterns[] is a list. A wall sit is an isometric held in a squat position; recording only one loses either the joint position or the fact that nothing moved.
